questions.q: Name a Shakespeare play
questions.policy: The 37-39 plays usually attributed to Shakespeare, including collaborations (The Two Noble Kinsmen, Edward III). Poems are not plays.

questions.q: Name a character from a Shakespeare play
questions.policy: Named characters who appear in Shakespeare's plays (Puck, Malvolio, Lady Macbeth). Real historical kings count when they appear as characters.

questions.q: Name a stage musical
Name a classical composer
questions.policy: Composers of Western art music from medieval to contemporary, including film and opera composers.

questions.q: Name a genre of music
Name a musical instrument
questions.policy: Instruments from any tradition, including electronic ones. The voice doesn't count.

questions.q: Name an art movement
Name a famous painter
questions.policy: Real painters known for their art. Surnames alone are fine when clear (Turner, Monet).

questions.q: Name a famous painting
Name a novelist
questions.policy: Real people who have published novels. Surnames alone are fine when clear (Dickens, Austen).

questions.q: Name a book (by its title)
questions.policy: Published books of any kind - novels, children's books, non-fiction, poetry collections. Series names don't count (name one book).

questions.q: Name a children's author
questions.policy: Real authors best known for books for children or teenagers.

questions.q: Name a poet
questions.policy: Real poets, from any era or language.

questions.q: Name a Beatles song
questions.policy: Songs released by the Beatles, including covers they recorded and released.

questions.q: Name an opera
questions.policy: Operas and operettas, including Gilbert and Sullivan.

questions.q: Name a type of dance
Name a typeface or font
Name a type of knot
Name a type of boat or ship
questions.policy: Kinds of vessel (not individual named ships).

questions.q: Name a type of hat
Name a type of shoe
questions.policy: Kinds of footwear, including boots, slippers, sandals and well-known brands people use as names (Crocs, Doc Martens).

questions.q: Name an item of clothing
Name a piece of furniture
Name a tool you'd find in a toolbox
questions.policy: Hand tools and small power tools you could reasonably keep in a toolbox.

questions.q: Name a kitchen utensil or gadget
Name a job that wears a uniform
Name a job title ending in -er
questions.policy: Real occupations whose usual title ends in -er (baker, plumber, astronomer). Hobbies and roles that aren't jobs don't count.

questions.q: Name a type of station, other than a train station
questions.policy: Anything properly called a station - police station, space station, weather station, workstation, Radio 1 isn't, but a radio station is. Train and railway stations are excluded.

questions.q: Name a currency, past or present
questions.policy: Current national currencies, historical currencies (drachma, groat, guinea) and well-known cryptocurrencies. Coins and slang (quid) count as aliases of their currency.

questions.q: Name a language
questions.policy: Natural languages, living or dead, plus constructed languages with real speakers (Esperanto, Klingon). Every language with an ISO 639-3 code counts.

questions.q: Name a programming language other than Python or JavaScript
questions.policy: Languages used to write programs, including query and scripting languages (as listed by GitHub Linguist). Markup and data formats like HTML and JSON are not programming languages.

questions.q: Name a social media platform or messaging app, past or present
Name a key on a computer keyboard
questions.policy: Labelled keys on a standard PC or Mac keyboard, excluding the letter and number keys themselves.

questions.q: Name a computer file extension
questions.policy: File name extensions in real use (.docx, .mp3, .py). The dot is optional.

questions.q: Name a car manufacturer
questions.policy: Car makes past or present, from anywhere (DeLorean, Reliant and Saab count).

questions.q: Name an airline
questions.policy: Passenger or cargo airlines, current or defunct.

questions.q: Name a UK high-street shop, past or present
questions.policy: Shop chains that have traded on British high streets, including ones that have gone (Woolworths, BHS, Our Price).

questions.q: Name a supermarket chain
questions.policy: Supermarket and grocery chains anywhere in the world, current or defunct.

questions.q: Name something you'd find in a museum
Name something you'd pack for a beach holiday
Name something you'd find in a kitchen
Name something you'd find in a garden shed
Name something you'd find at the seaside
Name something you'd see at a wedding
Name something with wheels
Name something you can recycle
Name a job or profession
questions.policy: Paid occupations, current or historical (chimney sweep, lamplighter, data scientist).

questions.q: Name a fruit
questions.policy: Culinary and botanical fruits both count, so tomato, cucumber and chilli are in. Named apple and pear varieties count.

questions.q: Name a vegetable
questions.policy: Plants or parts of plants eaten as vegetables, including pulses, roots, leaves and named varieties.

questions.q: Name a cheese
questions.policy: Named cheeses and cheese styles from anywhere. Brand names count if they're a cheese (Babybel, Dairylea).

questions.q: Name a type of pasta
questions.policy: Pasta shapes and noodle types used as pasta, including filled pastas. Dishes (carbonara, bolognese) are sauces, not pasta types.

questions.q: Name a herb or spice
questions.policy: Culinary herbs and spices, fresh or dried, including blends like garam masala.

questions.q: Name a type of bread
questions.policy: Breads, rolls, flatbreads and named loaves from anywhere in the world.

questions.q: Name a type of cake
questions.policy: Named cakes, sponges, tortes and traditional bakes called cakes.

questions.q: Name a British biscuit
questions.policy: Biscuits made or widely sold in Britain - classics, brands and homemade types. Jaffa Cakes count (legally cakes, but everyone files them with the biscuits).

questions.q: Name a cocktail
questions.policy: Named cocktails and mixed drinks.

questions.q: Name a type of tea
questions.policy: Teas, tea blends and herbal infusions people call tea.

questions.q: Name a coffee drink
questions.policy: Coffee drinks and preparations from anywhere.

questions.q: Name a curry or Indian dish
questions.policy: Curries from anywhere plus dishes from the Indian subcontinent, including breads, sides and sweets.

questions.q: Name a fish you can eat
questions.policy: Fish species eaten by people somewhere in the world. Shellfish don't count.

questions.q: Name a pizza topping
Name a sauce or condiment
questions.policy: Sauces, dressings, relishes, pickles, dips and table condiments.

questions.q: Name a way to prepare potatoes
questions.policy: Cooking methods and named potato dishes (chips, mash, boulangère, rösti, clapshot).

questions.q: Name a type of breakfast cereal
questions.policy: Breakfast cereals, by brand or type (porridge and muesli count).

questions.q: Name a flavour of crisps
questions.policy: Flavours sold on crisps (potato or otherwise) in Britain, now or in the past.

questions.q: Name a chocolate bar
questions.policy: Chocolate bars and countlines sold in Britain, now or in the past.

questions.q: Name an ingredient of a full English breakfast
questions.policy: Things that turn up on a cooked British or Irish breakfast plate, including regional extras (laverbread, haggis, potato scones).

questions.q: Name a dessert or pudding
questions.policy: Sweet courses from anywhere - puddings, tarts, ices, custards, pastries served as dessert.

questions.q: Name a national or regional dish
questions.policy: A named dish strongly tied to a country or region (paella, haggis, pho, feijoada). Generic foods like soup or salad don't count.

questions.q: Name a nut or edible seed
questions.policy: Culinary nuts and edible seeds. Peanuts count even though they're legumes.

questions.q: Name a style of beer
questions.policy: Recognised beer styles (bitter, porter, saison, gose), not brands.

questions.q: Name a type of sandwich
questions.policy: Named sandwiches and sandwich fillings people order by name (BLT, Reuben, chip butty, banh mi, croque monsieur).

questions.q: Name a recurring household bill
questions.policy: Regular bills or payments a household pays, from utilities and insurance to subscriptions and fees.

questions.q: Name an animal that stings
questions.policy: Animals with a sting: insects, scorpions, jellyfish and their relatives, stingrays, venomous fish with spines, and so on.

questions.q: Name a living bird bigger than a chicken
questions.policy: Bird species alive today whose adults are clearly larger than a domestic chicken.

questions.q: Name a place or landmark with Great or Grand in its name
questions.policy: Real places, natural features and landmarks whose name contains "Great" or "Grand" (or Grande).

questions.q: Name something you empty regularly at home
questions.policy: Things around the home that get emptied as a routine: bins, appliances, containers and so on.

questions.q: Name a method of advertising
questions.policy: Ways businesses get their message in front of people, old and new.

questions.q: Name any item or block in Minecraft
questions.policy: Items and blocks from Minecraft, any version, by their in-game names.

questions.q: Name something people keep in a wallet or purse
questions.policy: Things people commonly or plausibly carry in a wallet, purse or card holder.

questions.q: Name something with a handle
questions.policy: Objects that have a handle (or a handle as a name, if you can justify it).

questions.q: Name something in a first-aid kit
questions.policy: Things found in or reasonably kept in a first-aid kit.

questions.q: Name something that flies but isn't a bird
questions.policy: Anything that flies or is flown: insects, mammals, machines, toys, objects and more. Birds don't count.

questions.q: Name a word that goes before "house"
questions.policy: A word that forms a familiar compound or phrase with "house" after it, written as one word or two (greenhouse, haunted house).

questions.q: Name something with stripes
questions.policy: Animals, objects, flags, patterns and anything else known for stripes.

questions.q: Name something you could find in space
questions.policy: Natural objects, phenomena and human-made things out in space.

questions.q: Name something you would find at a funfair
questions.policy: Rides, games, food, stalls and people at a travelling fair or theme-park style funfair.

questions.q: Name something that is orange
questions.policy: Things that are typically orange in colour.

questions.q: Name an excuse for being late
questions.policy: Any reason people give (true or not) for turning up late.

questions.q: Name a country in Africa
questions.policy: The 54 African UN member states and the Sahrawi Republic, plus historical African states and empires (Carthage, Rhodesia, Mali Empire). Former names (Zaire, Swaziland) are aliases of today's countries.

questions.q: Name a country in Asia
questions.policy: Sovereign states usually counted as Asian, including the Middle East. Russia and Turkey count (they span Europe and Asia). Egypt doesn't.

questions.q: Name a country in Europe
questions.policy: Sovereign European states (including Russia, Turkey and the Caucasus), plus England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

questions.q: Name a landlocked country
questions.policy: Sovereign states with no coastline on the open sea. Countries on the Caspian (Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan) count as landlocked.

questions.q: Name a country whose name ends in the letter E
questions.policy: Common English names of sovereign states ending in E. Official long forms count if they end in E too.

questions.q: Name a country whose name starts with the letter S
questions.policy: Common English names of sovereign states starting with S. Scotland counts.

questions.q: Name a country whose name has exactly four letters
questions.policy: Common English names of sovereign states with exactly four letters.

questions.q: Name a country whose name ends in the letter A
questions.policy: Common English names of sovereign states ending in A.

questions.q: Name a country with a double letter in its name
questions.policy: The country's common English name must contain the same letter twice in a row (Greece, Philippines, Morocco). Spaces don't join letters.

questions.q: Name a country with a Mediterranean coastline
questions.policy: The 21 sovereign states with a Mediterranean coast (Gibraltar is British territory, not a country).

questions.q: Name an island that isn't an independent country
questions.policy: Any named island or island group that is not itself a sovereign state - Skye, Greenland, Sicily, Tasmania, Hawaii. Islands that are whole countries (Iceland, Jamaica, Malta) don't count.

questions.q: Name an island
questions.policy: Any named island or island group, anywhere, including island countries.

questions.q: Name a volcano
questions.policy: Named volcanoes, active or extinct, on Earth or elsewhere (Olympus Mons counts). Arthur's Seat and Edinburgh's Castle Rock are extinct volcanoes.

questions.q: Name a river
questions.policy: Any named river or major stream. Typing 'River' before or after the name is fine.

questions.q: Name a lake
questions.policy: Named natural lakes, lochs, loughs and llyns, plus large reservoirs. 'Lake' or 'Loch' before or after the name is optional.

questions.q: Name a mountain
questions.policy: Named mountains and summits anywhere, including British hills that are commonly called mountains. Ranges don't count (say a peak).

questions.q: Name a desert
questions.policy: Named deserts, hot or cold. Antarctica counts as a desert.

questions.q: Name a capital city
questions.policy: Capitals of sovereign states, plus the capitals of the UK's home nations, US states, Canadian provinces and Australian states, and former national capitals (Bonn, Rio de Janeiro, Kyoto).

questions.q: Name a city in Europe
questions.policy: Any European town or city with a population of 15,000 or more (GeoNames data), plus well-known smaller cities. Russia west of the Urals and Turkey's European side count.

questions.q: Name a city in the USA
questions.policy: Any US city or town of 15,000 people or more (GeoNames data), plus notable smaller towns. 'New York City' and 'New York' are the same answer.

questions.q: Name a UK city or town
questions.policy: Any city or town in the United Kingdom with 15,000 people or more, plus officially designated cities of any size (St Davids, Wells).

questions.q: Name a British place ending in -chester, -cester or -caster
questions.policy: Towns, villages and cities whose names end in -chester, -cester or -caster, mostly from the Latin castra (a Roman fort).

questions.q: Name an English county
questions.policy: Historic, ceremonial or former administrative counties of England (Rutland, Avon, Cumberland, Middlesex all count).

questions.q: Name a county or council area of Scotland or Wales
questions.policy: Historic counties, current council areas and principal areas of Scotland and Wales (Fife, Powys, Gwynedd, Kincardineshire).

questions.q: Name a US state
questions.policy: The 50 states. Washington DC and Puerto Rico are not states.

questions.q: Name a London landmark
Name a London Underground station
questions.policy: Stations served by the Tube, plus closed 'ghost' stations. DLR-only, Overground-only, Elizabeth line-only and National Rail stations are rejected with a note.

questions.q: Name a London Underground line
questions.policy: The 11 Tube lines, plus lines that have been absorbed or renamed (Metropolitan's East London line, the Hammersmith branch). The DLR, Overground lines and Elizabeth line are not Tube lines.

questions.q: Name a famous bridge
Name a British or English monarch
questions.policy: Kings and queens regnant of England, Scotland, Great Britain or the UK, from the Anglo-Saxons on. Numbers optional (Henry VIII, Henry 8). Lady Jane Grey counts.

questions.q: Name a Roman emperor
questions.policy: Emperors of Rome and of the Western and Eastern (Byzantine) empires, including co-emperors and short-lived usurpers recognised by historians. Julius Caesar was dictator, not emperor.

questions.q: Name a US president
questions.policy: The 45 people who have served as President of the United States.

questions.q: Name a British prime minister
questions.policy: The people who have served as Prime Minister of Great Britain or the UK, from Robert Walpole to the present.

questions.q: Name a Greek god or goddess
questions.policy: Deities of Greek myth - Olympians, Titans, primordials, nymph-goddesses and minor gods. Roman names are rejected with a note.

questions.q: Name a Roman god or goddess
questions.policy: Deities of Roman religion and myth, including those borrowed from the Greeks under Roman names.

questions.q: Name a Norse or Egyptian god or goddess
questions.policy: Deities of Norse or ancient Egyptian religion.

questions.q: Name a mythical creature
questions.policy: Creatures from myth, legend and folklore anywhere in the world. Creatures invented for modern fiction don't count (no Pokémon).

questions.q: Name an ancient civilisation or people
questions.policy: Civilisations, empires and peoples of the ancient world (before about AD 500) anywhere, plus the pre-Columbian civilisations of the Americas, which are conventionally called ancient (Aztecs, Incas). Vikings and Anglo-Saxons are medieval, so they don't count.

questions.q: Name a famous battle
questions.policy: Named historical battles and sieges, on land, sea or in the air.

questions.q: Name a war
questions.policy: Named historical wars, including civil wars and short conflicts with an established name.

questions.q: Name a famous explorer
questions.policy: Real explorers and navigators, from antiquity to space.

questions.q: Name a famous ship
questions.policy: Individual named ships, real or fictional (HMS, RMS and similar prefixes optional).

questions.q: Name a book of the Bible
questions.policy: Books of the Old and New Testaments, plus the Apocrypha/Deuterocanonical books (Tobit, Judith, Maccabees).

questions.q: Name a famous person known by just one name
questions.policy: Real people best known by a single name - singers, footballers, artists, historical figures. Religious figures aren't included.

questions.q: Name a city that has hosted the Olympic Games
questions.policy: Host cities of the Summer or Winter Olympics, past or confirmed future (Brisbane 2032).

questions.q: Name a famous horse (real or fictional)
Name a saint
questions.policy: People recognised as saints by a major Christian church (the 'St' is optional).

questions.q: Name something that is yellow
Name something that is cold
Name something people are afraid of
Name something associated with Christmas
Name something with a shell
questions.policy: Animals, foods and objects that have a shell, in any accepted sense - tortoise, egg, pistachio, taco, a Unix shell, an artillery shell.

questions.q: Name something that is round
Name something that comes in pairs
Name something that has keys
questions.policy: Anything that has keys in a real sense - instruments, keyboards, locks, maps (a key to the symbols), Florida (the Keys), databases, codes.

questions.q: Name something that has a trunk
Name something that has teeth (but isn't an animal)
questions.policy: Objects with teeth or toothed edges - saws, combs, zips, gears, rakes, a Venus flytrap's leaves, a dandelion (dent de lion).

questions.q: Name a colour that is also the name of a fruit
Name a shade of blue
Name something that is green
Name a breed of dog
questions.policy: Recognised breeds and long-established types count (Labradoodle and other popular crosses too). General words like puppy or mongrel don't.

questions.q: Name a breed of cat
questions.policy: Recognised cat breeds. Coat patterns (tabby, tortoiseshell, calico) are not breeds.

questions.q: Name a breed of horse or pony
questions.policy: Horse and pony breeds and established types. Colours (palomino, roan) are not breeds.

questions.q: Name an insect
questions.policy: True insects (six legs as adults), including larval names like caterpillar and maggot. Spiders, scorpions, woodlice and centipedes are not insects.

questions.q: Name a shark
questions.policy: Any shark species or common shark name, including dogfish and catsharks.

questions.q: Name a type of whale, dolphin or porpoise
questions.policy: Any cetacean. Orcas are dolphins, so they count. Whale sharks are fish, so they don't.

questions.q: Name an Australian animal
questions.policy: Animals native to Australia (including its seas). Introduced species like rabbits and camels don't count.

questions.q: Name a bird of prey
questions.policy: Raptors - hawks, eagles, falcons, kites, buzzards, harriers, ospreys, vultures, owls and secretary birds, by species or group.

questions.q: Name a reptile or amphibian
questions.policy: Any reptile (lizards, snakes, turtles, crocodilians, tuatara) or amphibian (frogs, toads, newts, salamanders, caecilians). Extinct reptiles count too.

questions.q: Name a flower
questions.policy: Flowering plants grown or known for their flowers, wild or cultivated.

questions.q: Name a type of mushroom or fungus
questions.policy: Mushrooms, toadstools, moulds, yeasts and other fungi, by species or common name. Lichens count (they're part fungus).

questions.q: Name a tree native to Britain
questions.policy: Trees that colonised Britain naturally after the last Ice Age. Sycamore, horse chestnut and sweet chestnut were introduced, so they don't count.

questions.q: Name a bird you might see in a UK garden
questions.policy: Wild birds that regularly visit British gardens, including flyovers like gulls and swifts.

questions.q: Name a dinosaur
questions.policy: Named dinosaur genera, plus birds' extinct relatives that are dinosaurs. Pterosaurs (pterodactyls) and marine reptiles (plesiosaurs) are not dinosaurs.

questions.q: Name a noise an animal makes
questions.policy: Words for animal calls and sounds, including spelt-out noises (moo, ribbit) and verbs (bray, bellow).

questions.q: Name a collective noun for animals (e.g. a murder of crows)
questions.policy: Recorded collective nouns for groups of animals, traditional or modern. Type the noun (parliament) or the whole phrase (a parliament of owls).

questions.q: Name an animal whose name is exactly four letters long
questions.policy: Any animal (species, group or breed) whose usual English name has exactly four letters.

questions.q: Name a marsupial
questions.policy: Pouched mammals - kangaroos, wallabies, koalas, wombats, possums, opossums, bandicoots, quolls and relatives.

questions.q: Name a bird
questions.policy: Any bird, by species or familiar group name (finch, gull, owl). Extinct birds like the dodo count.

questions.q: Name a fish
questions.policy: Any fish, freshwater or sea, by species or common name. Shellfish, whales and jellyfish are not fish.

questions.q: Name a mammal
questions.policy: Any mammal, wild or domestic, living or extinct. Whales, bats and platypuses count.

questions.q: Name a snake
questions.policy: Any snake species or common snake name.

questions.q: Name a tree
questions.policy: Any tree, by common or species name, from anywhere in the world.

questions.q: Name an animal whose name contains another animal
questions.policy: The letters of a different animal's name must appear unbroken inside the answer, as a word or hidden inside one - catfish (cat), elephant (ant), beagle (eagle), lemur (emu).

questions.q: Name a planet, moon or dwarf planet
questions.policy: Planets, named moons and dwarf planets of our solar system, named exoplanets, plus famous fictional planets (Krypton, Tatooine), which count as witty answers.

questions.q: Name a chemical element
questions.policy: The 118 named elements. Symbols are accepted as aliases (Fe for iron).

questions.q: Name a chemical element whose symbol is one letter
questions.policy: The 14 elements with single-letter symbols: H, B, C, N, O, F, P, S, K, V, Y, I, W, U.

questions.q: Name a chemical element named after a place or a person
questions.policy: Elements whose names honour a real place (country, city, region, continent, village) or a real person. Mythological figures and planets don't count.

questions.q: Name a bone in the human body
questions.policy: Named human bones and standard anatomical names for groups (metacarpals, vertebrae). Common names are fine (collarbone, kneecap).

questions.q: Name an organ of the human body
questions.policy: Organs in the anatomical sense - structures with a specialised job, including skin, glands and parts of the brain with organ status. Tissues like blood and bone in general don't count.

questions.q: Name a muscle in the human body
questions.policy: Named human muscles, by anatomical or everyday name (biceps, glutes, quads).

questions.q: Name a type of cloud
questions.policy: Cloud genera, species and named varieties, plus well-known cloud phenomena (mammatus, noctilucent, contrails).

questions.q: Name a constellation
questions.policy: The 88 official constellations, by Latin or English name. Well-known asterisms (the Plough, Orion's Belt) are accepted with a note.

questions.q: Name a star (other than the Sun)
questions.policy: Individual named stars. Constellations and galaxies don't count.

questions.q: Name a gemstone or precious mineral
Name a type of rock
questions.policy: Named rocks (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic). Minerals that form whole rocks also count.

questions.q: Name a mineral
questions.policy: Naturally occurring minerals recognised by geologists, by name or common name (fool's gold for pyrite).

questions.q: Name a unit of measurement
questions.policy: Units for any quantity - length, mass, time, energy, data, money excluded. Abbreviations are accepted as aliases (km).

questions.q: Name a unit of measurement named after a person
questions.policy: Units named after a real person (watt, newton, kelvin, decibel via the bel for Alexander Graham Bell).

questions.q: Name a shape
questions.policy: Two- or three-dimensional geometric shapes and well-known named shapes (crescent, heart, star).

questions.q: Name a famous scientist
questions.policy: Real scientists, mathematicians and inventors known for scientific work. Surnames alone are accepted where clear.

questions.q: Name a phobia (by its proper name)
questions.policy: Recorded -phobia words naming a fear, from dictionaries or established usage (arachnophobia, triskaidekaphobia).

questions.q: Name a branch of science
questions.policy: Recognised scientific disciplines and sub-disciplines, natural or social (astrophysics, seismology, ethology).

questions.q: Name something invented by someone British
questions.policy: Inventions credited to British (or then-British) inventors - the jet engine, the World Wide Web, the cat's eye, the sandwich.

questions.q: Name a James Bond film
questions.policy: The Eon Productions Bond films, plus the 1967 Casino Royale and Never Say Never Again.

questions.q: Name a Bond villain
Name a Disney animated film
questions.policy: Animated features released by Disney, including Pixar films.

questions.q: Name a Pixar film
questions.policy: Feature films made by Pixar Animation Studios. Shorts don't count.

questions.q: Name a Disney villain
Name a film whose title is a single word
questions.policy: Feature films whose full title is one word (Jaws, Titanic, Up, Alien). Numbers count as words, so Se7en is fine but Jaws 2 isn't.

questions.q: Name a film directed by Steven Spielberg
questions.policy: Feature films Spielberg directed (including TV films like Duel). Films he only produced, like Back to the Future, don't count.

questions.q: Name a film director
questions.policy: Real people who have directed a feature film.

questions.q: Name a Marvel Cinematic Universe film
questions.policy: Films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (from Iron Man in 2008). Sony's Spider-Man and X-Men films are not MCU.

questions.q: Name a superhero
questions.policy: Costumed heroes from comics, film and TV, by hero name or secret identity.

questions.q: Name a superhero team
questions.policy: Teams of heroes from comics, film, TV and games - the Avengers, the Incredibles, Thunderbirds' International Rescue.

questions.q: Name a Pokémon
questions.policy: Any of the official Pokémon species, all generations.

questions.q: Name a Harry Potter character
questions.policy: Named characters from the Harry Potter books and films (and Fantastic Beasts). First or last names alone are fine when they point to one character.

questions.q: Name a character from The Simpsons
Name a Doctor Who villain or monster
Name a British sitcom
questions.policy: Situation comedies made for British TV or radio.

questions.q: Name a famous detective (fictional)
Name a fictional wizard or witch
Name a children's TV show
Name a TV soap
Name a TV quiz or game show
Name a famous duo
Name a board or card game
Name a sport played with a ball
Name an Olympic sport
questions.policy: Sports and disciplines in the Summer or Winter Olympics, now or in the past (tug of war, cricket in 1900).

questions.q: Name an Olympic sport in which Great Britain has won a medal
questions.policy: Sports (not individual events) where Team GB or earlier British teams have won at least one Olympic medal, Summer or Winter, 1896 to 2024.

questions.q: Name a sport that doesn't use a ball
questions.policy: Recognised sports and competitive activities played without any ball - rowing, fencing, curling, darts, ice hockey (a puck isn't a ball).

questions.q: Name a martial art
Name an English football club
questions.policy: Clubs in the English football pyramid down to step 6, past Football League members, and famous non-league sides. Welsh clubs in English leagues (Cardiff, Swansea, Wrexham) count.

questions.q: Name a club that has played in the Premier League
questions.policy: The clubs that have played at least one Premier League season since 1992-93.

questions.q: Name a footballer who has played in the Premier League
questions.policy: Anyone who has made a Premier League appearance since 1992. Data covers every player with minutes from 2016-17 onward plus famous earlier players; surnames alone work when unambiguous.

questions.q: Name a winner of the men's or women's Ballon d'Or
questions.policy: Winners of the Ballon d'Or (men's since 1956, women's since 2018), including the FIFA Ballon d'Or years 2010-15.

questions.q: Name a country that has won the FIFA World Cup (men's or women's)
Name a Wimbledon singles champion
questions.policy: Winners of the men's or women's singles at Wimbledon, from 1877 on.

questions.q: Name a Formula One world champion driver
Name an NBA player, past or present
questions.policy: Anyone who has played in the NBA (data from the official NBA player list). Surnames alone work when unambiguous.

questions.q: Name an NFL player, past or present
questions.policy: Anyone listed in the nflverse player database (modern era and many earlier players).

questions.q: Name an NBA, NFL or MLB team
questions.policy: Current franchises in the NBA, NFL or MLB, by full name or nickname.

questions.q: Name a fielding position in cricket
